definition: For a meromorphic function G near s0, Res(G;s0) is the coefficient of (s-s0)^(-1) in the Laurent expansion.
equivalents: contour integral: (2pi i)^(-1) integral_C G(s) ds
examples: if F has simple pole r/(s-s0), then Res(F(s)x^s;s0)=r x^s0
counterexamples: substituting s=s0 into a pole is invalid
a zero of the numerator may cancel an apparent pole
translation_to_pvg: hybrid/nonlocal: residues act on analytic transforms built from decoded arithmetic coefficients, not directly on valuation coordinates
claim_ceiling: identity and finite symbolic verification only

definition: For counterclockwise rectangle with right c, left sigma, height T: integral_right + integral_top + integral_left_down + integral_bottom = 2pi i sum residues.
equivalent_shift: integral_right_up = integral_left_up + 2pi i sum residues - integral_top - integral_bottom
counterexamples: using left side upward without changing sign

authorization_rule: syntactic completeness is necessary but not sufficient; every field requires a proof-grade source before CERT authorization

rule: total error must name each component, parameter dependence, norm, domain, and limiting process
counterexamples: writing O(error) without defining the parameter
letting T->infinity before proving horizontal decay
combining conditionally convergent zero sums without convention

rules: counterclockwise closed contour gives +2pi i residues
left side of a counterclockwise rectangle is traversed downward
rewriting left integral upward introduces a minus sign
worked_check: right_up - left_up + top_left + bottom_right = 2pi i residues

statement: PVG supplies coefficient geometry and labelled prime-power support; contour geometry, Laurent expansions, residues, and boundary estimates belong to a complex-analytic layer.
loses: local point identity after global contour aggregation
claim_ceiling: PVG reinterpretation does not certify contour estimates or new theorems
